answer.text: Erosion of purchasing power over time

explanation.text: The Logic: Source pp.16-17 and p.22 describe inflation as the loss of purchasing power and the erosion of the real value of money over time, so inflation risk is the risk that real returns are eroded even when nominal returns are positive. The Trap: Interest-rate, currency, and credit risks are distinct risk categories per the workbook, not inflation risk. Note: Real return equals nominal return adjusted for inflation; that adjustment is what inflation risk threatens.
